title: [Chapitre] III. Réseaux via découpages : notes manuscrites (08/06/1986).

errors: The equivalence 'a,b distinct and comparable ⇔ ∃c strictly between a and b' needs density (Grothendieck flags this: 'utilise divisibilité'). Without density the ⇐ direction holds but ⇒ fails.

R determines the order only up to reversal on each connected 'branch' or component. The margin note about arbitrary choices acknowledges this. The lemma as stated ('structure biordonnée connue') is correct only in that sense.

The text characterising disjointness says 'c entre a et b', yet its first quantifier reads '∃c tel que c...'. It is consistent, but the page is a draft and the axioms for R are never actually listed ('Axiomes?' is left blank).

ideas.what: A total (dense) order up to reversal is equivalent to its strict betweenness relation; the order is recovered after fixing an oriented pair (a,b).
ideas.modern_name: Betweenness relations / axiomatics of linear betweenness

ideas.what: Comparability of distinct elements characterised via existence of an intermediate element, using density.
ideas.modern_name: Dense orders; comparability expressed through betweenness

ideas.what: Orientation choices are independent on each component, so the order is determined only up to reversal per component.
ideas.modern_name: Orientations of comparability/betweenness structures (cf. Gallai's transitive orientations)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gallai (1967); Pitcher–Smiley (1942) on betweenness in lattices/posets

deep.surprise_reason: A routine, classical lemma: an order up to reversal is the same thing as its betweenness relation. It is used here as a technical step in Grothendieck's unpublished combinatorial 'réseaux/découpages' project. It is of archival interest only.
transcription_corrections: 'biogon[?] biordonnée[?] et connue' should read 'binaire biordonnée est connue' (or similar): '...structure de [binaire] biordonnée est connue quand on connaît la relation...'.
'pour L binaire[?]' likely reads 'pour L binaire' (the 'binaire' objects being dense linear pieces).
'(utilise divisibilité! des [-?-] binaires)' reads '(utilise divisibilité! des binaires)', with a struck-out word in between.
'pour longue[?]' probably reads 'par hypothèse' or similar, but is uncertain.
The left-margin 'Il existe des choix arbitraires' reads roughly 'Il existe des ... de choix arbitraires dans ...'.
